citation: "Kinzie Street Bridges." Chicagology. Transcribing A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, Volume I (1886), and carrying a tabulated chronology of the six Kinzie Street bridges.

transcribes.work: A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, Volume I — the passage on Samuel Miller's 1832 bridge over the North Branch
transcribes.note: Carries the location near the south-east corner of Kinzie and Canal, the stringer construction, and the 1833 reading that the structure was 'useless for teams'. A compilation from pioneer testimony — rung 3, and the rung this record claims. The tabulated bridge chronology beside it is the page's own editorial apparatus, not Andreas, and is not declared here.

note: The Andreas passage transcribed here is the fullest statement reached about the first bridge over the North Branch: 'In the summer of 1832 Samuel Miller, the original possessor of the old ferry scow, built the first bridge over the North Branch. It was located near the southeast corner of Kinzie and Canal streets, in the vicinity of the present bridge of the Chicago & Northwestern Railroad Company. It was formed of stringers and only fitted for foot passengers. Even up to the summer of 1833 the structure was useless for teams.' The page also carries a table of the Kinzie Street crossings whose first row — 'Kinzie #1, 1832, 1839, Wood, Fixed, Bent, builder Samuel Miller' — is the only statement reached about when this bridge ended. THE TABLE IS THE PAGE'S OWN EDITORIAL SUMMARY, not Andreas, and its 'Bent' type-word is a modern classification applied across six bridges spanning a century; it is not a period description and is treated as weaker than Cleaver's eyewitness account of the abutments. Tier 3 for the Andreas transcription; the surrounding apparatus is a finding aid.
